purpose: Versioned successor to package 1.2.0. Adds T20 to distinguish elapsed age since a past milestone from any future horizon. The age is descriptive only and must never be classified as INMEDIATO, CORTO, MEDIO, or LARGO. All entities and events are fictional; this fixture does not establish empirical validity, real market behavior, causal impact, or human inter-evaluator agreement.

cases.unit: Fictional protocol ALPHA technical and operational functions only; public-token market valuation, reputation, attention, and demand are outside this declared unit.
cases.scenario: A website branding announcement is evaluated only for a material effect on ALPHA's declared technical and operational functions; no conclusion is made about the public token or market perception.

evidence.content: The complete reviewed architecture inventory for the declared technical and operational unit lists no contract, governance, custody, validator, API, liquidity, access-control, deployment, or operational dependency on the rebranded website.

The inventory covers all technical and operational components and the complete announcement scope for the declared unit as of the cutoff; the unit expressly excludes public-token market valuation, reputation, attention, and demand.

The reviewed deployment, configuration, access-control, service-status, and incident records show no change to the declared technical or operational functions attributable to the website branding announcement by the cutoff.

expected.direction: INDETERMINADA unless separate evidence supports NEUTRAL
expected.reason: The reviewed evidence rules out a material mechanism only within the explicitly bounded technical/operational unit. It makes no I0 claim about token-market, reputational, attention, or demand effects.

cases.unit: Fictional exchange BETA support desk
cases.scenario: A short interruption affects one non-critical support endpoint; a substitute is claimed to be available.

evidence.content: One support endpoint is unavailable; trading, custody, deposits, withdrawals, and settlement remain operational.
A documented alternate support channel accepts the affected request class at the measured test load.
The affected user population can authenticate and access the alternate channel.

expected.reason: The indirect effect is local and bounded; availability, capacity, and access of the substitute are evidenced.

cases.unit: Fictional exchange GAMMA institutional deposit segment
cases.scenario: A deposit-processing component fails for one institutional segment; deposits remain uncredited beyond their documented processing window and cannot be used within that segment while the restriction persists.

evidence.content: The affected component directly processes deposits for the identified institutional segment only; the component map lists no dependency for other customer segments.

At the cutoff, 27 deposit requests belonging to 11 institutional accounts remain uncredited for four hours after the service's documented processing window; the source records identify each request and its pending state.

The 11 affected accounts cannot use the uncredited deposits as exchange balances for trading or collateral while the requests remain pending; withdrawals from already credited balances and other exchange functions remain available.

The affected accounts belong to one identifiable institutional segment; no evidence establishes that this segment or this deposit path is central to the exchange as a whole. The counts and duration are fictional case facts, not universal intensity thresholds.

expected.observed_effect: Deposits are uncredited beyond the documented processing window and unavailable for the segment's exchange use at the cutoff.
expected.potential_effect: The restriction may continue while the component remains unavailable; duration beyond the observed four hours is not established.
expected.reason: A direct, observed and functionally consequential restriction supports a material but bounded change for the declared segment. The evidence does not establish broad or central exposure at exchange level.

cases.unit: Fictional protocol DELTA oracle-dependent application ecosystem
cases.scenario: A shared oracle degrades across a defined ecosystem: four of five listed applications suspend new lending and borrowing because their price-feed freshness condition is breached; existing positions and essential access remain protected by documented fallback controls.

evidence.content: The frozen ecosystem inventory contains five named applications; four depend on the same oracle publication path for the price feed used to authorize new lending and borrowing. The fifth application does not use that path.

Oracle telemetry records price-feed updates older than the applications' documented freshness condition for 38 consecutive minutes at the cutoff; the four dependent applications record the condition as breached.

Application logs confirm that new lending and borrowing are suspended in the four dependent applications while the freshness condition remains breached. This is an observed change to a material operating capability across the declared ecosystem, not merely a generic degraded-service label.

Existing positions remain queryable; the documented secondary feed continues to support the safety checks for existing positions; withdrawals and user access remain available. The evidence does not show compromise of custody, settlement, essential access, protocol viability, or a system-wide shutdown.

The five-application inventory is complete for the declared ecosystem at the cutoff. The four affected applications are central components of that defined ecosystem; no claim is made about applications outside it.

expected.direction: NEGATIVA for the declared affected ecosystem
expected.observed_effect: New lending and borrowing are suspended in four of the five inventoried applications at the cutoff.
expected.potential_effect: The suspension persists only while the oracle freshness condition remains breached; duration beyond the observed interval is not established.
expected.reason: The complete denominator and shared dependency support broad/central exposure within the declared ecosystem, and application logs establish a material operating-condition change. The documented fallback preserves existing positions and essential access, so I4 is not supported.

cases.unit: Fictional custody network EPSILON withdrawal authorization service
cases.scenario: A confirmed compromise of the sole authorization path threatens essential access to customer assets.

evidence.content: A forensic report confirms compromise of the sole authorization service.
No independent authorization path exists for the declared custody unit.
The compromised service is required for withdrawals; the report documents threat to essential customer access.

expected.reason: A concrete, evidenced mechanism threatens an essential access function.

cases.unit: Fictional cryptoasset market segment ZETA
cases.scenario: A rumor alleges that a widely used infrastructure provider may stop supporting the segment, but no mechanism evidence is available.

evidence.content: An anonymous post claims the provider may discontinue support.
No verified dependency inventory, provider statement, or operational evidence connects the provider to the declared segment.

expected.reason: Wide potential exposure cannot compensate for an unverified speculative channel.

cases.unit: Fictional protocol ETA bridge withdrawal function
cases.scenario: If a pending technical condition triggers an emergency withdrawal pause, the sole withdrawal function would be unavailable.

evidence.content: The bridge has one withdrawal function and no alternative route for the declared unit.
The documented emergency condition activates a withdrawal pause.
The triggering condition has not been confirmed as of the cutoff.

expected.intensity: I4 for the explicitly conditional scenario
expected.reason: Potential severity within a defined scenario is separate from the probability or confirmation of its condition.

cases.unit: Fictional asset THETA with separately defined user segments A and B
cases.scenario: The same integration event produces independently evidenced, materially different consequences for two separately defined THETA user segments; neither segment's effect is used to offset the other's classification.

evidence.content: Segment A consists of users whose declared settlement workflow routes through integration R; the frozen workflow inventory and prior successful transaction records show R is the only supported route for that workflow.

After the event, integration R rejects Segment A workflow requests; transaction logs show the defined settlement workflow cannot complete for the affected requests, and no alternative route is available to that segment at the cutoff.

Segment B consists of users whose declared marketplace execution workflow previously had no supported route to the named venue; the frozen integration inventory documents that limitation before the event.
After the event, integration R becomes available to Segment B; successful transaction logs confirm that the previously unavailable defined workflow completes through R.

Segments A and B are separately defined by their workflow dependency and evidence populations. The case does not define a market-wide aggregate or a common denominator for combining them. The consequences are material to the respective declared workflows but do not threaten essential access or viability.

segment_A.observed_effect: The declared settlement workflow is unavailable for the affected Segment A requests; no alternative route is evidenced.
segment_A.reason: Direct loss of the only supported route causes a concrete, bounded functional restriction in the declared segment.

segment_B.observed_effect: The previously unavailable declared marketplace workflow completes successfully through the newly available integration.
segment_B.reason: Direct availability of the integration enables a concrete, bounded workflow capability in the declared segment.

expected.aggregate: Do not assign an aggregate classification: no aggregate unit or common denominator is defined. MIXTA is permissible only in a later, explicitly defined aggregate evaluation that independently retains both segment effects; never average or cancel them.
expected.reason: The integration's relevance and the observed consequences are evidenced independently for each segment. Segment classifications remain separate; neither effect establishes a global asset-level impact.

cases.unit: Fictional protocol IOTA validator population
cases.scenario: Two evidence items disagree on whether the affected validator population is broad.

evidence.content: Report A asserts broad validator exposure but does not disclose its denominator.
Report B provides contrary validator records and disputes broad exposure.
No approved source-credibility rule resolves this conflict.

expected.reason: Preserve the contradiction; do not select a source by authority or majority.

cases.unit: Fictional exchange KAPPA withdrawal queue
cases.scenario: An exchange announces a recovery route for an existing withdrawal restriction, but deployment, capacity, and user access are not demonstrated by the cutoff. This case tests mitigation handling only.

evidence.content: The exchange says a recovery route is being prepared.
No deployment record, capacity test, or user-access evidence exists by the cutoff.
The original withdrawal restriction remains documented.

expected.rule: Do not reduce a baseline intensity established in a separate, sufficiently evidenced evaluation; this case does not supply or imply that baseline.
expected.reason: The announcement is not proof of deployment, operational availability, capacity, or access. The continued restriction is recorded, but its baseline intensity is not classified in this mitigation-only test.

cases.unit: Synthetic elapsed-time boundary test
cases.scenario: Measure exact durations from a precise reference instant.

expected.reason: Upper endpoints are inclusive at 24 h, 7 × 24 h, and 90 × 24 h.

cases.unit: Synthetic elapsed-time boundary test
cases.scenario: Measure one second beyond each exact boundary.

expected.reason: The first instant after each upper endpoint belongs to the next category.

cases.unit: Synthetic event milestone
cases.scenario: A source provides a calendar date only, and classification depends on the exact time.

evidence.content: The event is scheduled for 2026-01-11; no time or timezone is provided.

expected.reason: Do not assume midnight or a local timezone.

cases.unit: Synthetic phased governance event
cases.scenario: An event has distinct announcement, approval, effective, and implementation milestones.

expected.reason: Do not collapse announcement and implementation into one horizon.

cases.unit: Synthetic uncertain event time
cases.scenario: The available event-time interval straddles the 24-hour horizon boundary.

expected.reason: Preserve the full interval and compatible categories.

cases.unit: Fictional protocol LAMBDA incident classification under a single-human-owner evaluation process with an AI-assisted adversarial review.
cases.scenario: The sole human owner records a primary assessment of the frozen evidence packet. After that record is sealed, an AI assistant in an isolated context receives only the same packet and a predefined challenge prompt. The AI may identify overlooked evidence, ambiguity, or alternative interpretations; it is not a second human evaluator and its output is not inter-evaluator evidence.

evidence.content: The common fictional packet describes a direct operational restriction and contains a disputed statement about whether the affected function is central.
The project has exactly one human owner/evaluator. The process must not require a second human participant or represent an AI system as a human evaluator.

The human's first-pass assessment is recorded and sealed before an AI challenge. The AI receives the frozen packet without the human's result, preferably in an isolated conversation, and returns a structured critique with evidence references and uncertainty.

expected.human_primary_assessment: The sole human owner records the first-pass direction, intensity, horizons, conditions, evidence references, and rationale before seeing any AI critique; preserve timestamp, protocol version, and package hash.
expected.ai_review: An AI assistant may perform a separate structured challenge using the same frozen evidence packet and a predefined prompt. It is an auxiliary analytical review, not a human evaluator, not a vote, and not an independent inter-rater.
expected.separation: Do not provide the human's primary conclusions to the AI during its first challenge pass. Use an isolated context where practical; record whether isolation was achieved and any contamination risk.
expected.provenance: Record the AI product/model/version when available, execution date, exact prompt or prompt version, evidence packet hash, output, and unavailable metadata explicitly as NOT_AVAILABLE rather than inventing it.
expected.disagreement_handling: Compare the AI critique with the sealed human assessment. Classify each difference as overlooked evidence, evidence interpretation, unit/scope, anchor ambiguity, temporal reasoning, or AI error. The human owner retains decision authority, documents the rationale, and revises the methodology only through a versioned change; never average or claim consensus.
expected.fixture_limit: This workflow supports traceability and adversarial challenge in a single-human project. It cannot establish inter-evaluator reliability, human consensus, or independent human agreement. The fixture contains no simulated human or AI evaluation outputs.

cases.unit: Fictional asset MU exposure to a proposed protocol change
cases.scenario: Available information is incomplete and cannot confirm or rule out a material mechanism.

evidence.content: A proposal references a change but omits affected contracts and implementation details.
No complete dependency inventory or operational confirmation is available.

expected.reason: Missing essential information is not evidence that the mechanism is absent.

cases.unit: Synthetic elapsed-time daylight-saving test
cases.scenario: Compare two Europe/Madrid local timestamps across the 2026 spring daylight-saving transition.

expected.reason: Compare absolute instants; preserve original offsets and IANA timezone.

cases.unit: Synthetic event milestone with contradictory source timestamps
cases.scenario: Two sources place the same milestone on opposite sides of the 24-hour boundary.

expected.reason: Preserve both source timestamps and the 23 h 50 min–24 h 10 min interval; do not choose one without an approved rule.

cases.unit: Synthetic past milestone age classification boundary
cases.scenario: A fictional milestone occurred before the evaluation cutoff. The elapsed age must be retained as descriptive chronology and must not be mapped to a future horizon category.

expected.reason: The milestone occurred before the cutoff. Record the exact elapsed age for chronology and audit, but do not assign INMEDIATO, CORTO, MEDIO, or LARGO: those categories describe a remaining duration to a future target or another explicitly defined prospective measurement, not the age of a completed event.

change_log.change: Narrow the declared unit to technical and operational functions; explicitly exclude token-market, reputation, attention, and demand outcomes from this I0 test.
Add observed processing delay, affected request/account scope, and the concrete inability to use uncredited deposits within the defined segment.
Specify the dependency denominator, affected application functions, observed degradation, and continuity boundary that prevents an I4 inference.
Add independent evidence of the integration's role and distinct observed consequences for each segment; retain separate classifications.
Explicitly mark baseline intensity as NOT_ASSESSED; test only that an unverified mitigation cannot attenuate a separately established baseline.

Replace the two-human-evaluator dependency in T16 with a single-human primary assessment and a separately recorded AI-assisted adversarial review. AI is explicitly not a human evaluator and cannot establish inter-evaluator reliability.
Adds a dedicated past-milestone case. Elapsed age is calculated from occurrence to evaluation cutoff and retained as descriptive-only; future horizon categories are explicitly not applicable.
